title: Noise Criterion vs. Noise Rating and dB(A)
description: Comparing Noise Criterion (NC, NCB, RNC) to Noise Rating (NR) and dB(A). Determines appropriate noise criteria for different room types and occupancy levels.

components.content:
## Noise Criterion vs. Noise Rating and dB(A)

[Noise Criterion](nc-noise-criterion-d_725.html "nc noise criterion") - _[NC](nc-noise-criterion-d_725.html "nc noise criterion")_ - were established in U.S. for rating indoor noise, noise from air-conditioning equipment etc.

In Europe it is common to use [Noise Rating Curves](nr-noise-rating-d_60.html "nr noise rating curves") - _[NR](nr-noise-rating-d_60.html "nr noise rating curves")_.

[dB(A)](decibel-d_59.html "decibel dBA dBB dBC") _- LA_ - is a weighted method compensating for the human hearing of sound pressure at different frequencies.

Choosing appropriate noise criteria is important when specifying acceptable levels of noise.

rows: Very quiet - Concert and opera halls, recording studios, theaters
Private bedrooms, theaters, TV/radio studios, conference rooms, libraries
Private living rooms, board rooms, hotel bedrooms
Quiet - Public rooms in hotels, offices, classrooms, courtrooms
Moderate noisy - Drawing offices, bathrooms, reception areas, lobbies, stores
Noisy - Kitchens, laundry rooms, computer rooms, supermarkets
